Pick the right extinguisher for a live electrical fire, then find the signed way out.
Burning: the conveyor motor starter panel. The supply is still live.
A fire has started in this room. The starter panel feeding the conveyor motor is alight and its supply has not been isolated, so treat everything inside it as live.
Three extinguishers are stored nearby. Only one is safe on a live electrical fire; the other two conduct the current back to whoever is holding them. Identify the right one by the colour of its body.
Then get out. Put the exit sign at the real way out of the room you are standing in, and take the route that leads to it.
Point the phone at the floor beside the real way out of this room, then tap to put up the exit sign.
Tap a clear patch of floor. An extinguisher will appear there, and you will not be told which one.
Tap the floor to lay down an escape route arrow. Spread the three of them out in different directions.
Too close to something already placed. Leave about a metre between objects.
Tap the extinguisher you would use on this fire.
Tap the arrow that leads to the exit sign.
That is not one of the extinguishers. Tap one of the three bottles.
Tap one of the escape route arrows.
You will need that exit, but the extinguisher decision comes first.
The black CO₂ extinguisher. Carbon dioxide does not conduct electricity and leaves no residue, so it is safe on live equipment and will not write off the panel.
The red water extinguisher. Water conducts, so a jet onto a live panel carries the current straight back up the stream to you. Water is for wood, paper and cloth, never for electrical fires.
The cream foam extinguisher. Foam is mostly water, so it conducts as well. Foam is for flammable liquids such as fuel, oil and solvents, not for live equipment.
That extinguisher is not rated for this fire.
That arrow leads away from the exit sign. In smoke you will not be able to see the door, so the signage is all you have, and a route that ignores it is a dead end.
This attempt will not be scored or saved.
You picked the right extinguisher and followed the signage. Run the drill again from time to time: in real smoke there is no time to work it out.
Read the explanations again before you retry. The colour of the body tells you what is inside: black is CO₂, cream is foam, red is water.
Master step-by-step fire extinguisher operation: Pull safety pin, Aim at base, Squeeze lever, and Sweep side-to-side.
When operating a fire extinguisher, always remember the PASS rule: Pull the safety pin, Aim low at the base of the fire, Squeeze the operating lever, and Sweep side-to-side.
First verify that the pressure gauge needle is in the GREEN zone, indicating the cylinder is fully pressurized and ready for use.
In this module, you will place the realistic fire extinguisher in AR and perform each step interactively.
Tap a clear patch of floor to place your 3D fire extinguisher.
Step 1: Inspect the pressure gauge. Is the gauge needle in the GREEN zone?
Step 2 (P - Pull): Pull out the yellow safety pin to break the tamper seal.
Step 3 (A - Aim): Aim the nozzle low, directly at the base of the fire (the fuel source).
Step 4 (S - Squeeze): Squeeze the operating handle firmly to release extinguishing agent.
Step 5 (S - Sweep): Sweep the nozzle side to side across the base of the fire.
Gauge needle is in GREEN zone (Ready)
Gauge needle is in RED zone (Low Pressure)
Aim low at base of fire (Fuel)
Sweep side to side (%1$d of %2$d passes completed)
Before using any extinguisher, check that the pressure gauge needle is in the green zone so you know it is fully charged.
Good check! The needle is in the green zone, indicating optimal pressure.
A red-zone gauge indicates low pressure or discharge. Always inspect the gauge before relying on an extinguisher.
Safety pin pulled and tamper seal broken. The handle is now unlocked and ready to discharge.
Aiming at the base of the fire targets the burning fuel directly to stop combustion.
Aiming at the top of flames wastes extinguishing agent. Always aim low at the fuel source at the base of the fire.
Firm pressure on the handle opens the internal valve and releases the extinguishing agent.
Great job! You successfully mastered the PASS method: Pull, Aim, Squeeze, and Sweep!
You demonstrated full mastery of the PASS method (Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep). Remember to inspect equipment regularly before entering high-risk areas.
Review the PASS steps and try again. Always pull the pin first, aim at the base of the fire, squeeze the handle, and sweep across the flames.
